title: Choose Synod's command composition
question: All three use the approved Mission Control Veil world and keep the presenter prominent. Which composition should carry into the application?

options.label: Cinematic Split
options.thesis: The council chair and the decision console share the viewport as equal protagonists.
options.viewport: Presenter fills the left half; prompt, controls, and action occupy the right; mission route anchors the bottom.
options.risk: The split can feel static if the route and video states do not carry motion.

options.label: Briefing Window
options.thesis: The presenter opens the session, then the command shelf pulls the user directly into the decision flow.
options.viewport: A full-width presenter window dominates the top; one continuous composer shelf and route sit directly beneath.
options.risk: The vertical sequence uses more height before the live council workspace appears.

options.label: Flight-Path Workspace
options.lineage: Mission plotting table × optical command visor
options.thesis: One luminous route physically connects the user's question, council chair, deliberation, and verdict.
options.viewport: Decision controls form a left rail; the presenter dominates upper right; live council and verdict share the lower plane.
options.risk: The asymmetric geometry requires careful mobile adaptation and disciplined information density.
